title: Est: your first Latin sentences
subtitle: Lesson 1 · Sentences with est – no articles
intro: Welcome to Latin! Today's seven words are among the most common in the language (*et* 'and' is the single most frequent Latin word, *est* 'is' the second). With them you can already make real sentences like *Puella est bona* – 'The girl is good.'

vocab.notes: Today you only need *est* 'is' (and *nōn est* 'is not'). The other forms of this verb come in later lessons.
Put it right before the word it negates: *nōn est* 'is not'.
Describing a feminine noun such as *puella* it ends in -a: *bona*.
With feminine nouns: *magna*. Of a person it means 'tall' or 'great'.

grammar.title: est – and no 'the'
grammar.body:
*est* means 'is': *Puella est bona* = 'The girl is good.'

Latin has **no words for 'the' or 'a'**. *puella* can mean 'girl', 'the girl' or 'a girl' – choose whatever sounds natural in English.

An adjective that describes a feminine noun like *puella* or *fēmina* also ends in **-a**: *puella bona* 'a good girl', *fēmina magna* 'a tall woman'.

Word order is flexible and the verb likes to come last: *Puella bona est* and *Puella est bona* both mean 'The girl is good.'

*nōn* 'not' goes right before the word it negates: *Puella nōn est magna* 'The girl is not big.'

grammar.title: Saying it out loud
grammar.body: Classical Latin is pronounced the way it is spelled. **c** is always hard (k), **v** sounds like English w, every vowel is pronounced, and a line over a vowel (ā, ē, ō) just means it is long: *fēmina* = FAY-mi-na, *nōn* = NOHN. *puella* is stressed pu-EL-la: the double l makes that syllable heavy, so it takes the stress.

examples.la: Iūlia nōn est fēmina; Iūlia est puella.
examples.en: Julia is not a woman; Julia is a girl.
The girl is good and tall.

exercises.prompt: Choose the Latin for: The girl is good.
Translate into Latin: Julia is a girl.
Translate into Latin: Rome is great.

reading.title: Iūlia et Cornēlia
reading.la: Iūlia est puella. Iūlia est puella bona. Cornēlia nōn est puella; Cornēlia est fēmina. Fēmina magna et bona est. Rōma est magna.
reading.en: Julia is a girl. Julia is a good girl. Cornelia is not a girl; Cornelia is a woman. The woman is tall and good. Rome is great.
reading.hint: Every word here is from today's list (plus the names Julia, Cornelia and Rome).

notes: Frequency: *et* is #1, 'to be' (dictionary form sum) #2 and *nōn* #6 in the DCC core list of the 1,000 most common Latin words.
